questions.question: True or False: If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix, then \(\lambda\) is real.

paragraphs: Every real symmetric matrix has only real eigenvalues.

questions.question: True or False: Every square matrix does not satisfy its own characteristic equation.

paragraphs: Cayley–Hamilton states that every square matrix does satisfy its own characteristic equation. Therefore the negative statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of an orthogonal matrix, then \(1/\lambda\) is also an eigenvalue.

paragraphs: For orthogonal \(A\), \(A^{-1}=A^T\). The eigenvalues of \(A^{-1}\) are reciprocals of those of \(A\), while \(A^T\) has the same eigenvalues as \(A\). Hence the reciprocal also occurs in the spectrum.

questions.question: True or False: The eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are just the diagonal elements of the matrix.

paragraphs: The characteristic determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal factors.

questions.question: True or False: The sum of the eigenvalues of \(A\) equals the trace of \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&3&-1\\0&-1&3\end{bmatrix}\).

paragraphs: For every square matrix, the sum of eigenvalues (with algebraic multiplicity) equals the trace. Here the trace is \(7\).

questions.question: Find the quadratic form corresponding to \(\begin{bmatrix}2&0&-2\\0&2&1\\-2&1&-2\end{bmatrix}\).

paragraphs: Using \(Q=X^TAX\), the diagonal terms are \(2x^2+2y^2-2z^2\); symmetric off-diagonal terms contribute \(-4xz+2yz\).
